washing-machine:tripping-electrics.text: An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
washing-machine:tripping-electrics.hazard: Dangerous wiring or an insulation fault (repeated tripping, a burning smell or scorch marks); water present raises shock risk.
washing-machine:tripping-electrics.applicability: Appliance repeatedly trips the electrics, or there is a burning smell / scorching.

tumble-dryer:overheating.text: Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
tumble-dryer:overheating.hazard: Overheating in a dryer is a fire risk; the most common contributor is restricted airflow (lint).
tumble-dryer:overheating.applicability: This fault (overheating). If it smells of burning, escalate to stopping use.

tumble-dryer:filter-blocked.text: Clean the lint filter after every load — a build-up of fluff is a fire risk and restricts airflow. Don't run the dryer overnight or while you're out.
tumble-dryer:filter-blocked.hazard: Lint build-up is a fire risk; restricted airflow causes overheating.
tumble-dryer:filter-blocked.applicability: This fault (blocked filter / restricted airflow); always.

oven-cooker:tripping-electrics.text: An oven that keeps tripping your electrics, or smells of burning, may have an electrical fault. Stop using it and switch it off at the fuse box / consumer unit (ovens are often wired in, not plugged), don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician.
oven-cooker:tripping-electrics.hazard: Dangerous wiring or an insulation fault; ovens are frequently hard-wired, so isolation is at the consumer unit rather than a plug.
oven-cooker:tripping-electrics.applicability: Oven trips the electrics, or there is a burning smell / scorching.

hobs:gas-burner.text: If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.
hobs:gas-burner.hazard: An unsafe gas appliance or a gas escape.
hobs:gas-burner.applicability: Gas appliance where the customer can smell gas or suspects the appliance is unsafe.

microwave:not-heating.text: Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
microwave:not-heating.hazard: High-voltage capacitor and internal circuitry can retain a dangerous charge even after the microwave is unplugged; contact can cause a severe or fatal electric shock.
microwave:not-heating.applicability: Any microwave internal-repair situation for this fault, independent of which internal part has failed.
